Issued at 138 AM MST Sat Nov 14 2026

Above normal temperatures and mostly quiet weather will prevail 
across much of the Cowboy State this weekend. For Saturday, a 
nearing trough will try to bring some precipitation chances to 
portions of southern and western WY. However, due to it being so
unorganized and the bulk of the energy tracking farther south, 
much of the state will remain dry. A few rain/snow showers 
cannot be ruled out this morning into the early afternoon hours 
today. The best chances (30-60%) will be across far 
southwestern and western WY with lesser chances elsewhere. The 
higher elevations of western WY may see a very light coating of 
snow, but overall accumulations will be little to nonexistent. 
Locations east of the Divide will remain dry with breaks in the 
cloud cover by the afternoon likely allowing for sunshine to 
break through. Temperatures will be in the mid to upper 50s 
east of the Divide and mid to upper 40s west of the Divide. 
Sunday is looking quite nice with clouds decreasing, allowing 
for plenty of sunshine throughout the day. Temperatures are 
expected to remain around the same values as Saturday. Winds do 
look to increase across the Wind Corridor by the afternoon from 
Rock Springs to Casper. Speeds of 15 to 25 mph with gusts of 30 
to 40 mph will be likely during the afternoon. 

The start of the work week will see pleasant, dry, and mild 
conditions continue across the region. Temperatures will be similar 
to Sunday with breezy winds once again expected in the afternoon 
from Casper to Rock Springs. Another disturbance looks to be on the 
horizon for late Tuesday afternoon into Wednesday. This disturbance 
is in association with a trough that digs across the western CONUS 
starting late Monday. However, energy with this trough is likely to 
struggle to organize as it tracks east throughout the day Tuesday. 
Models do not really show any well defined closed low developing 
which will limit impacts. Precipitation chances overall do look much 
better than this most recent system, especially for the higher 
elevation mountains and western WY. Along with better precipitation 
chances, this disturbance will bring cooler and seasonable 
temperatures to the area.

The current forecast is for showers to move into western WY 
late Tuesday behind a cold front that will gradually sweep west 
to east over the region. Temperatures may be a little too warm 
for snow to initially fall for the western valleys, but they 
should cool quite quickly allowing for a transition over to 
snow. Snow showers will be possible through the overnight 
Tuesday into Wednesday across portions of western and southern 
WY. Some precipitation may make it across the Divide, but 
dynamics may not be the most favorable. So at this time the best
chances for precipitation will remain over western and southern
WY along with the higher elevation mountains of western, 
central, and northern WY. Winds are another aspect to monitor as
initially models showed a potent area of 700mb winds move over 
central WY. However, the recent trends have lowered these winds.
With that being said, some gusty winds of 30 to 40 mph still 
look possible Tuesday afternoon along the Wind Corridor from 
Rock Springs to Casper. As for snow accumulations, probabilistic
guidance is showing western valleys having a 30-60% chance of 
at least 1 inch of snow. The higher elevations of the Teton, 
Gros Ventre, Wyoming/Salt River, and western Wind River Ranges 
have a 50-70% of 3 or more inches of snow accumulation. Other 
high elevations such as the Absaroka and Bighorn Ranges have a 
20-50% chance of seeing 3 inches. Models are trying to show the
chance for light snowfall across the lower elevations of 
central and northern WY. However, the dynamics are not very 
favorable as mentioned before so chances for any snow 
accumulation at this time look very low. The system moves out by
Wednesday afternoon, leaving behind much colder temperatures. 
If any snow accumulation does occur overnight, temperatures may 
be even colder than what is currently forecast. Currently 
Wednesday nights lows look to get into the 20s east of the 
Divide and teens west of the Divide. As mentioned earlier, 
if snow accumulation does occur especially for western valleys 
these lows could be even colder. There remains the potential for
another possibly more potent system to impact the region by the
end of the work week into the weekend. However, being so far 
out and with how volatile the current set up is it's tough to 
know what to expect at this time. Long range models continue to 
flip-flop with not much consensus at this time. So, stay tuned 
as it is looking like the upcoming work week may be quite 
eventful for the Cowboy State.
